corrected_value.title: Effects of immediate-reinforcement training on delay discounting behavior in rats

decisions.quote:
A group of rats was exposed to an immediate (no-delay)-

reinforcement intervention and subsequent delay discounting

behavior was modestly, but statistically signiﬁcantly, more

impulsive compared to a control group. This is consistent

with previous work (Fox, 2022; Fox etal., 2019; Renda

etal., 2018; Smith etal., 2022), and with the conclusion
that prolonged exposure to immediate reinforcement may

have just modest impacts on subsequent impulsive choice,

compared to relatively larger impacts of exposure to delayed

reinforcement. This was true in the present experiment

despite double the number of subjects in each group and

double the number of immediate reinforcement training tri-

als, compared to previous research (Fox 2022; Fox etal.,

2019).
decisions.reason: Omitted replication target (no prior adjudication file existed). Fox (2024) is titled a systematic replication of immediate reinforcement training on delay discounting behavior in rats and uses the author's prior FR 2 immediate-reinforcement training vs. maturation/handling control and posttest signaled-RIFI delay-discounting paradigm. In the Introduction (lines 135-160) and Discussion (lines 524-549), the author explicitly identifies Fox (2022) (10.1002/jeab.727) and Fox et al. (2019) (10.1016/j.beproc.2018.11.009) as the previous research whose sample size per group and number of immediate-reinforcement training trials were doubled (with a 50% longer intervention duration) to test the limits and generality of their reported results, and compares the observed modest increase in impulsive choice directly against them. Shipped row 1480 covers only Renda et al. (2018) (10.1002/jeab.432), leaving Fox (2022) omitted.

decisions.reason: Neither parenthetical citation placement nor omission from the doubling-protocol benchmark alone excludes Smith et al. (2022; 10.1016/j.beproc.2022.104584), but primary inspection of Smith et al. shows Fox (2024; 10.1007/s40732-024-00597-x) does not retest any Smith-specific empirical finding. Fox (2024) compares 47-day FR 2 immediate reinforcement (n = 24) against an untreated handled/maturation control group (n = 24) on posttest signaled-RIFI delay discounting, explicitly benchmarking its doubled sample and training trials against Fox (2022) and Fox et al. (2019). In Smith et al. (2022), Experiment 1 (N = 36) compared delayed-FI (FI 5 s/FI 30 s) against No-Delay (FI 0 s, functionally FR 2) across adjusting-delay (ADJ) and systematic-delay (SYS) tasks with no handled/maturation control: ADJ showed no intervention effect (PSE 15.5 vs. 15.9 s), and SYS showed fewer LL choices in delayed-FI than ND at middle delays alongside a steeper ND choice slope. Experiment 2 (N = 48) tested pre/post 5-s vs. 10-s delayed-FI combinations with no ND group. Smith et al.'s General Discussion cites Fox (2021/2022; 10.1002/jeab.727) for the claim that ND exposure increases impulsivity relative to maturational controls. Thus, Fox (2024) retests the ND-versus-maturational-control finding of Fox (2022), Fox et al. (2019), and Renda et al. (2018; shipped row 1480), citing Smith et al. (2022) only for broad thematic consistency.
